title: The First Dream
journal: Vosh-Leera has a second task for me. She asked me to come to her house in Jal-Veesa for it.
objectives: Ask Vosh-Leera for her second task. (marker: Vosh-Leera)

plan.going: I work for the Toh-Reel-Ka through Vosh-Leera; the trees are sick and nobody knows why.
plan.next: Ask Vosh-Leera, in her house, for the second task.

answers: I am Tarin, freed from the Owing barge. Vosh-Leera works for the Toh-Reel-Ka, a secret order of the Xeech-Leel. Trees are sickening along the river and they want to know why. The Hist at Jal-Veesa is sick too.
Go to Vosh-Leera house in Jal-Veesa and ask her for her second task.
Enter her house and talk to her; I could also talk to Weeltul again about sap, scar, eggs and Umbriel.
I do not know the cause of the sickness, nor exactly what the Toh-Reel-Ka want from me. I could ask Vosh-Leera and Weeltul.

title: The First Dream
journal: Vosh-Leera gave me a cup of Jal-Veesa's sap, drawn before its scar closed. She told me that tree-minders drink sap to ask the trees a question. She wants me to ask where the sickness is. She wants me to drink it here, in front of her.
objectives: Drink the cup of sap in front of Vosh-Leera. (marker: Vosh-Leera)

plan.going: Sap drunk brings visions the trees send; Vosh-Leera wants me to ask the trees where the sickness is.
plan.next: Drink the cup in front of her, by telling her I will.

answers: Vosh-Leera, for the Toh-Reel-Ka, gave me a cup of Hist sap drawn before the scar closed. Trees are joined at the root, so drinking it lets me ask where the sickness is.
Drink the cup here in Vosh-Leera house, in front of her, then tell her everything I see.
Drink it now, or first talk to Weeltul or look at the cup; I could refuse, but she wants it done here.
I do not know what the sap will do to me or whether it is safe. I will find out by using it.

title: The First Dream
journal: I drank the sap and the world went black. I saw a young Hist among stilt huts beside a woven weir, and a reed hide beside a lone dead tree. Vosh-Leera is waiting to hear what I saw.
objectives: Tell Vosh-Leera what you saw. (marker: Vosh-Leera)

plan.going: The sap showed me a young Hist by a woven weir among stilt huts, and a reed hide by a lone dead tree.
plan.next: Tell Vosh-Leera what I saw, one thing at a time.

answers: I drank the sap and had a vision: a young grey Hist among pale stilt huts, a woven weir over a creek, and west of the weir a reed hide beside a lone dead tree with clay jars stacked in its shade. Vosh-Leera wants to hear all of it.
Tell Vosh-Leera what I saw, here in her house.
Talk to her and tell her; I can only report it.
I do not know which place this is (the weir could be Reed-Sill Weir, but I am not sure), or what the jars and the dead tree mean. Vosh-Leera may know.

title: The First Dream
journal: Vosh-Leera knew the place from what I told her. It is Teel-Fen Weir, a weir-wardens' camp south of Jal-Veesa, where a young Hist grew from the roots of Jal-Veesa's own. Heem-Jasa minds its tree there, and Vosh-Leera told me to see what she knows before I go near the hide.
objectives: Speak to Heem-Jasa at Teel-Fen Weir. (marker: Heem-Jasa)

plan.going: The vision showed Teel-Fen Weir, whose young Hist grew from Jal-Veesa's roots.
plan.next: Go south to Teel-Fen Weir and speak to Heem-Jasa, its tree-minder.

answers: The vision showed Teel-Fen Weir, a Sedge-Warden camp south of Jal-Veesa down the creek, where a young Hist grew from Jal-Veesa tree roots. Jars by a hide suggest someone is keeping sap. This may be where the sickness shows. I work for Vosh-Leera and the Toh-Reel-Ka.
Go to Teel-Fen Weir and speak to Heem-Jasa, its tree-minder, on the platform round the tree. Be careful at the hide.
Go straight to Heem-Jasa and ask her; or look around the camp or hide, but I was told to see Heem-Jasa first.
I do not know who the Sedge-Wardens are, who keeps the jars, or what is at the hide. I can ask Heem-Jasa.

title: The First Dream
journal: Heem-Jasa showed me her young tree's scar. It closed three nights ago over a grey paste that none of her people put there. Someone drained the tree and sealed it. Strangers who call themselves the Unbound keep jars at the reed hide by the lone dead tree west of the weir, the hide from my vision. I need to take what they have there. Heem-Jasa said I can go at them, shoot them from the reeds, or creep round to the hide's open side unseen; the hide has no door or lock, and if they see me they will fight.
objectives: Take the note from the reed hide west of Teel-Fen Weir. (marker: Note to the Sap-Takers)

plan.going: The young tree was drained and sealed with a grey paste by people, not by sickness. The strangers at the hide keep jars of sap.
plan.next: Go to the reed hide west of the weir and take the note lying with the jars; take a jar too.
plan.ways: Fight the three, shoot them from the reeds, or sneak to the west side of the hide and take the note unseen.
terms: the Unbound: topic.mn03-heem-scar: "people with no tree and no kin to answer to"

answers: Heem-Jasa tree was drained and its scar sealed with grey paste three nights ago, not by her people. Strangers calling themselves the Unbound, three Sap-Takers, keep jars at the reed hide west of the weir. This is likely tied to the sickness of the trees.
Take the note from the reed hide west of Teel-Fen Weir.
Fight them, shoot them from the reeds east of the hide, or creep round to the open west side unseen and take the note. If they see me they fight.
I do not know who the Unbound really are, who they answer to, or what the grey paste is. The note may tell me.

title: The First Dream
journal: I took the note from the reed hide. The crew's master orders them to bring their jars to Karsh-Naal Camp, and to seal every scar behind them. I should go back to Heem-Jasa on the platform and tell her.
objectives: Return to Heem-Jasa at Teel-Fen Weir. (marker: Heem-Jasa)

plan.going: The sap-takers drain trees and seal them on someone's orders, and carry the jars to Karsh-Naal Camp.
plan.next: Go back to Heem-Jasa, who will ask whether her tree will live.
plan.ways: Tell her the truth (it may die: she then trains me in Alchemy and sells to me) or a comfort (it will live: it eases her, but she will not train or trade with me).

answers: I took the note unseen. The crew master orders the Sap-Takers to bring their jars to Karsh-Naal Camp and seal every scar behind them. So someone organised draining and sealing trees.
Return to Heem-Jasa at Teel-Fen Weir and tell her.
Tell her what the note says, or read the note again; later perhaps go to Karsh-Naal Camp.
I do not know where Karsh-Naal Camp is, who the crew master is, or why they want sap. Heem-Jasa or Vosh-Leera may know.

title: The First Dream
journal: I told Heem-Jasa the truth, that her tree may die. She thanked me for not lying, and will teach me alchemy and sell me sap, fungus and eggshells. Next comes Karsh-Naal Camp, the Naga camp in the marsh east of Teel-Fen Weir, where the note sends the jars.

plan.going: I told Heem-Jasa the truth, that her tree may die. She thanked me for not lying, and will teach me alchemy and sell me sap, fungus and eggshells.
plan.next: Go to Karsh-Naal Camp, east of Teel-Fen Weir (MN04 marks it on the map).

answers: Someone, the Unbound Sap-Takers under a crew master, drain Hist trees, seal the scars with grey paste and take the sap to Karsh-Naal Camp. That is likely what sickens the trees. Heem-Jasa now trusts me.
Next is Karsh-Naal Camp, a Naga camp in the marsh east of Teel-Fen Weir. I should probably report to Vosh-Leera too.
Go to Karsh-Naal Camp, report to Vosh-Leera first, or buy and learn alchemy from Heem-Jasa.
I do not know who the crew master is, what the grey paste is, why they want sap, or what Naga means here. I could find out at the camp.
